about: Files where the graph's Score is not byte-for-byte the app's parseMusicXML Score (docs/GOALS/G02 §14.3, A32, A33). `node tests/scoregraph/tools/shadow-legacy.js --check` fails on any file not listed here, and on any listed file whose difference is not the one named. Two of these reasons -- microtone-rounded and transpose-sounds -- change which notes sound, on purpose: decision D7 (docs/GOALS/G02_SCORE_IMPORT.md §26) settled that the graph holds concert pitch and the old reader was wrong. The other three change no sounding note.

reasons.chord-head-order: A chord is one event with several heads, and the graph orders them low to high (canonical form, G01 §14.2). The app keeps the order the file wrote them in and marks every note but the first `chord: true`. Where a file writes a chord top down, the flag lands on a different note of the same chord. The same notes sound, at the same time, for the same length -- measured on all 17 files here (G02 §25 R2). It is not invisible, though: the flag decides which notes the leap estimate chains, so `Score.deriveSections` (App 3665) and `Coach.structural` (App 7916) can report a different widest leap, a different difficulty score and a different 'hard' flag -- on 6 of these files they do. The fingering search sorts each event by pitch (App 8523) and is unaffected; the other two readers of the flag (App 5414, 5788) only ask whether a bar has a chord at all.
reasons.ending-stop-without-start: A second-ending bracket that closes without opening. A ScoreGraph Ending has both ends (G01 §5.4), so the import reports the orphan and drops it; the app records it on the bar. The play order is the same - a stop alone opens nothing. Already allowlisted for the corpus round trip (tests/scoregraph/roundtrip-allowlist.json).
reasons.wedge-unpaired: A crescendo or diminuendo with one end missing. A ScoreGraph Wedge has both ends (G01 §5.10), so the import reports it and drops it; the app keeps the single end and ramps from or to it. Already allowlisted for the corpus round trip.
reasons.microtone-rounded: The file writes a quarter-tone <alter>. The notation side of a graph holds no floats (G01 §14.2), so the pitch is rounded away from zero for the notation and the value the file wrote is kept exactly in head ext, written back on export, reported as `W-IMPORT-MICROTONE`, listed in the import report's `normalized`, and marked `approx: 'microtone'` on the projected note (D7, G02 §26). The app truncates towards zero instead and says nothing. Nothing in the catalogue has a microtone.
reasons.transpose-sounds: A transposing part (<transpose>). MusicXML's <pitch> is what is written, not what sounds: a B-flat clarinet written C sounds B-flat. The graph stores concert pitch and the projection derives the printed pitch back into `writtenP`/`writtenMidi`, so the sheet draws C and the player sounds B-flat (D7, G02 §26). `parseMusicXML` has no notion of <transpose> and sounds the written note, which is simply wrong; this entry records that the graph is deliberately better, not that the two agree. The difference is `notes.set`, never `notes.order`. Nothing in the catalogue transposes.
